html:
Vardzia is a cave monastery cut into the cliff of Erusheti mountain above the Kura River in southern Georgia, founded under Queen Tamar and consecrated in 1185.

Its builders carved hundreds of rooms over many levels: cells, chapels, a church, wine cellars, bakeries and water tunnels, reaching deep into the rock. It was both a monastery and a fortress guarding the southern frontier against the Seljuks. The Church of the Dormition holds a fresco of Tamar herself. An earthquake in 1283 tore away the cliff face and exposed the rooms. The Persians plundered it in 1551. Monks again live in part of it, and it is one of the best known sights of Georgia.
sum: Vardzia is a cave monastery cut into the cliff of Erusheti mountain above the Kura River in southern Georgia, founded under Queen Tamar and consecrated in 1185.
